what_this_measures: Wire traffic on the MCP stdio pipe: the arguments of every tools/call request plus the results the server sent back, counted with o200k_base so the figure shares Tier 1's token basis.
what_this_does_not_measure: The tool-definition schema footprint of any client mode. The interposer cannot see what a client injected into the model's context as tool definitions (tier2-task-suites.md 4.3), and neither client's usage output isolates it, so no figure here converts a MODELED label in methodology-v0.md 3.2 or 3.3.
task_mix_caveat: Each figure is over the five scripted tasks for that server, three trials each, every trial counted including the ones that failed. A different task mix produces different call traffic for the same server (methodology-v0.md known limitation 5).
server_pin_caveat: The Tier 2 server pin is recorded per server below and is not asserted to be the same build as the Tier 1 row's pin. The github rows differ outright: Tier 1 measured the remote endpoint, Tier 2 ran the container.
small_n_rule: Absolute counts only, never rates. At three trials per task the per-trial values are the result and the median is the convenience on top (tier2-task-suites.md 3.3).

github.server_pin: ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server (container, no digest recorded by the runner)

meta_stripped_note: call_tokens_per_trial_meta_stripped is the same wire traffic with each tools/call result's top-level _meta member removed before counting. Some servers ride a protocol envelope there that one client requests and another does not: on this run github sent Claude Code a serverInfo block of roughly 1,400 tokens on every response and sent Gemini CLI none, so the raw github cells conflate server payload with envelope. A result with no top-level _meta counts identically in both columns, which is why only the github Claude Code cell differs.
